main_body: traditional Japanese two-story townhome (machiya) with tiled roof
top_band: blue-grey tiled roof slope and ridge (rows 0-30) and lower awning roof (rows 41-46)
evidence: The structure clearly shows the sloped top surface of the main roof (rows 0-30, 31 rows tall) and a secondary awning roof (rows 41-46, 6 rows tall), above the vertical upper plaster wall (rows 32-40) and ground floor wooden lattice wall and entrance (rows 48-77). Eave shadows (rows 31-32 and 47) and recessed windows/doorway are present.

style.evidence: While the roof tiles have 5 grey-blue shading steps, the pattern is mechanically repetitive across the entire width without the organic variation and per-tile contrast seen in the Beodeul roofs. The white plaster wall (rows 33-40) has very faint, barely perceptible two-tone variation rather than crisp speckle texture, and the wooden lattice strips and dark doorway interior (rows 61-71) contain large flat fills lacking wood grain or rich surface detail.
